title: Abelian-variety estimate
statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $g$ over a field $k$, let
$p=\operatorname{char}k$ and let $n\ge1$.

- **(a)** $[n]:A\to A$ is a finite flat surjective homomorphism, hence
an isogeny of degree $n^{2g}$; $A[n]=\ker[n]$ is a finite flat group
scheme over $k$ of order $n^{2g}$.
- **(b)** If $p>0$, then $A[p^e]$ is finite flat of order $p^{2ge}$ for
every $e\ge1$. If $n$ is prime to $p$ (in particular if $p=0$), then
$A[n]$ is finite étale of rank $n^{2g}$.
- **(c)** Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $n$ prime to $p$. Then
$A[n](k)\cong(\Z/n\Z)^{2g}$, and for every extension
$k\subseteq k'$ of algebraically closed fields the canonical map
$A[n](k)\to A[n](k')$ is an isomorphism.
- **(d)** Let $k$ be algebraically closed. Then $A(k)$ is a divisible
abelian group, $A(k)[n]\cong(\Z/n\Z)^{2g}$ for every $n$ prime to $p$,
and for every prime $\ell\ne p$
$$
T_\ell A\cong\Z_\ell^{2g},\qquad V_\ell A\cong\Q_\ell^{2g}.
$$

proof.text: *(a)* Let $n\geq1$. By [lem-sc-av-commutative] $A$ is a commutative group scheme, so by [lem-sc-mult-n-homomorphism](a) the map $[n]$ of [def-sc-mult-n] is a homomorphism of group schemes, acting on $R$-points by $x\mapsto nx$. By [lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat] (over the arbitrary field $k$) $[n]$ is finite and flat, $[n]_*\mathcal O_A$ is a locally free $\mathcal O_A$-module of rank $n^{2g}$, and the kernel $A[n]=A\times_{[n],A,e}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a finite group scheme of order $\dim_k\Gamma(A[n],\mathcal O_{A[n]})=n^{2g}$ ([def-sc-group-scheme]). Surjectivity: for $y\in A$ the fibre $[n]^{-1}(y)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(([n]_*\mathcal O_A)_y\otimes\kappa(y)\bigr)$, the spectrum of a $\kappa(y)$-algebra of dimension $n^{2g}\geq1$, which is a nonzero ring and so has a prime ideal; hence the fibre is nonempty. So $[n]$ is a surjective homomorphism with finite kernel, i.e. an isogeny in the sense of [def-sc-isogeny], whose degree, the order of its kernel, is $n^{2g}$. Finally $A[n]$ is flat over $k$ because every module over a field is free. (Stacks, Groupoids, Proposition 03RP parts (3) and (5), from Lemma 0BFG; the degree computation through $[n]^*\mathcal N\cong\mathcal N^{\otimes n^2}$ for a symmetric ample $\mathcal N$ is the proof of [lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat].)

source.place: Proposition 03RP (proposition-review-abelian-varieties), proof of parts (3) and (5); Lemma 0BFG (lemma-degree-multiplication-by-d)

proof.text:
*(b)* First clause: for $p>0$ and $e\geq1$ apply (a) with $n=p^e$: $A[p^e]$ is a finite flat group scheme of order $(p^e)^{2g}=p^{2ge}$. Second clause: let $n\geq1$ with $p
mid n$ (for $p=0$ every $n\geq1$). By (a), $A[n]$ is a finite flat group scheme over $k$ of order $n^{2g}$, and $p
mid n^{2g}$ since $p$ is prime (or $p=0$ and $n^{2g}
eq0$). By [lem-sc-mult-n-etale-kernel] (over the arbitrary field $k$, with $\operatorname{char}k
mid n$) $A[n]$ is étale over $k$; being finite of order $n^{2g}$, it is finite étale of rank $n^{2g}$ ([def-sc-group-scheme]). (The unit's argument for the étaleness, base change to $ ar k$, [lem-sc-fg-order-prime-etale] there and descent of étaleness, is the proof of [lem-sc-mult-n-etale-kernel]; in the Lean this is `AlgebraicGeometry.etale_torsionSubgroupScheme`, from `etale_of_not_dvd_finrankΓ` over any field.)

source.place: Proposition 03RP, proof of part (6): 'if n is invertible in k, then [n] is étale and hence A[n] is étale over k' (Lemma 0BFH)

proof.text: *(c)* Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $p\nmid n$. By (b), $A[n]$ is a finite étale group scheme over $k$ of order $n^{2g}$, so by [lem-sc-finite-etale-points] $\lvert A[n](k)\rvert=n^{2g}$ and, for every extension $k\subseteq k'$ of algebraically closed fields, the canonical map $A[n](k)\to A[n](k')$ is bijective; it is a group homomorphism (composition with $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ respects the group law on points), hence an isomorphism. The group structure $A[n](k)\cong(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}$ is [lem-sc-ntorsion-etale] (whose proof is the unit's: divisibility of $A(k)$, [lem-sc-divisible-group-structure] on each prime power $\ell^e\,\|\,n$, and the Chinese remainder theorem).

*(d)* Let $k$ be algebraically closed. The group $A(k)$ is abelian by [lem-sc-av-commutative] and divisible by [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective] ($x\mapsto nx$ is surjective on $A(k)$ for every $n\geq1$). For $n\geq1$ the $k$-points of $A[n]=A\times_{[n],A,e}\operatorname{Spec}k$ ([def-sc-mult-n]) are the $a\in A(k)$ with $[n](a)=e$, i.e. with $na=0$ by [lem-sc-mult-n-homomorphism](a); so $A(k)[n]=A[n](k)$, which for $p\nmid n$ is $\cong(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}$ by (c). For a prime $\ell\neq p$, $T_\ell A\cong\mathbf Z_\ell^{2g}$ and $V_\ell A\cong\mathbf Q_\ell^{2g}$ for the Tate modules of [def-wf-abelian-tate-module] is [prop-av-tate-rank].

source.place: Proposition 03RP, proof of parts (2), (4) and (7) ('A[ℓ](k) = A(k)[ℓ]'); the Tate module clause from prop-av-tate-rank
